guide.title: How to Use Policies
guide.description: Follow these 4 steps to set up content safety guardrails for your AI applications.

step1.title: Create a Policy
step1.description: Define rules to inspect LLM input/output. Choose block (stop the call), warn (allow but flag), or log (record only). Set scope to input, output, or both.

step2.title: Generate an API Key
step2.description: Create an API key to authenticate external systems calling the AIGP gateway. The key starts with aigp_ and is needed for the Playground and runtime integration.

step3.title: Test in Playground
step3.description: Paste your API key and send real prompts to verify your policies work as expected. See block/warn hits in real time.

step4.title: Review Evaluations
step4.description: View all policy hit history — which prompts were flagged, by which policy, and the matched text. Export to CSV for compliance reporting.

overview.subtitle: Run red-team adversarial tests against your connected AI models to automatically surface jailbreaks, prompt injection, bias, harmful content, privacy leaks and toxicity — then export auditable reports and model cards.

categories.jailbreak: Tricks the model into bypassing its safety guardrails
categories.prompt_injection: Hijacks model behavior via injected instructions
categories.bias: Detects bias and discrimination in outputs

overview.step1Body: Go to Evaluation Runs → New Run, choose a provider connection (the model under test), enter the model name, and select the risk categories to run.
overview.step2Body: Hit start — the Moonshot engine runs each category against its own datasets, asynchronously in the background. No need to wait.
overview.step3Body: The run detail page shows pass/fail live, the judgment and reason for every finding, and IMDA framework coverage. Generate a model card in one click.
